The range of θ=arctan⁡x is given by −90∘<θ<90∘.

Note that the angle θ spans the first and fourth quadrants.

Since −33 is negative, our answer is an angle that lies in the fourth quadrant, where the tangent is negative.

From the special values of the trigonometric functions and the oddness of the tangent function, we know that tan⁡(−30∘)=−tan⁡(30∘)=−33.

Since −30∘ lies within the range of arctan, we conclude that

arctan(−33)=−30∘.

Finally, we get 4arctan(−33)=4⋅(−30∘)=−120∘.
